dimensions.evidenceB: Elijah says he alone remains as a prophet of the LORD.

dimensions.evidenceA: The preservation is narrated during Jezebel’s killing of the prophets.
dimensions.evidenceB: The claim is spoken publicly at Carmel before the contest.
dimensions.label: Immediate setting

dimensions.evidenceA: The hidden prophets remain outside the Carmel count.
dimensions.evidenceB: At Horeb the LORD later names seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
dimensions.label: Later reply

evidence.observation: Obadiah took one hundred prophets, hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.
Elijah tells the people that he alone is left as a prophet of the LORD while Baal’s prophets number four hundred fifty.

record.tension: The narrative reports preserved prophets shortly before Elijah says that he alone remains as the LORD’s prophet.
record.title: In what sense is Elijah alone?
